task_name: SentinelMesh - Product demo and narration package
client_brief:
SentinelMesh is going in front of security buyers and we need the product cut. Be aware of what the pack actually holds: every supplied clip runs five seconds and none of them carry audio, so a narrated demonstration is not on the table. What we want is a short product film that lets the real screen captures do the work, with the cleared claims set as on screen text and each claim card held for at least two seconds over the screen that supports it, so a security engineer can read the interface detail that matters.

Please prepare
- Product demo master: 1 named export, 12 to 15 seconds, 16:9, under the supplied instrumental bed (sentinelmesh_bed.wav). The screen state on show must support the claim on screen at that moment, the claim wording must come from the cleared rows of the messaging sheet, one claim card is the security engineer's line “Catches the risky moment before a person clicks.”, and the film closes on the booking action.
- Product demo feed cut: 1 named export, 6 to 8 seconds, 1:1, silent, cut from the same material. The feature stays readable: crop the capture, never squeeze it; its one claim card repeats a claim card from the master over a screen state that supports it, and it closes on the booking action.
- Product website band and Website feature panel: not part of this round; deliver only the two cuts above.

House rules for this package
- No narration. The recorded read (sentinelmesh_vo.wav) stays out of these cuts, and no synthetic voice replaces it. The message is carried by on screen text.
- The approved closing action is set exactly as: Book a walkthrough. It is the last thing on screen on the master.
- Each cut shows the SentinelMesh shield mark at least once, on the Sentinel Navy ground, drawn as in the flat export of the mark on white.
- Each cut sets the product name “SentinelMesh” as type in the brand faces.
- Besides the product name and the closing action, only the Claim wording of rows marked Cleared in sentinelmesh_messaging.csv may appear on screen, word for word; the Proof Point column is background, not screen copy. The claim about cutting repeat risky behaviour by 60% is in legal review and must not appear anywhere.
- Precision over spectacle: no fear language, no exclamation, one idea per card.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage: looping one short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table. Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Catch the risky moment. Coach it away.
brand_identity.sector: Enterprise cybersecurity software (human cyber risk platform, SaaS)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Denver, Colorado. Roughly 40 people, venture-backed, entering its first full launch quarter.
brand_identity.about: SentinelMesh reduces human cyber risk for regulated enterprises. The platform watches for the risky moment, runs an adaptive simulation, and coaches the person in real time, closing the gap between security policy and daily behavior. We sell to CISOs and IT directors on annual contracts and we win on trust, precision, and proof that the product does what we say.
brand_identity.audience: CISOs, IT directors, and the security engineers reading over their shoulder at mid-market and enterprise organizations. Technical, skeptical, and short on patience for hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium enterprise. Annual contracts from 40,000 to 90,000 dollars. Everything we ship has to read as a considered purchase a security leader can defend internally, never as a self-serve consumer app.

brand_identity.typography: SentinelMesh runs a squared technical grotesque over a humanist sans, in four steps. Step 01, display, is PP Formula Condensed Medium at 84 px on 92 px leading, tracking -6 units, for the closing card on the 1920 frame, dropping to 64 px on the square cut and 28 pt in print. Step 02, the subheading, is PP Formula Condensed Medium at 56 px on 62 px leading, tracking -4 units, for claim cards, and it is the step that carries the signature: a 4 px Signal Cyan underscore beneath the line, overrunning the final letter by exactly one character width. Step 03, body, is Whitney Book at 34 px on 46 px leading, tracking 0, for lower thirds held to 65 characters a line, with print body at 9.5 pt on 14 pt. Step 04, fine print, is Whitney Book interface labels at 28 px on 38 px leading, tracking +10 units, with Whitney tabular figures on every number at every step. The cyan rule never appears twice in one frame.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, exact, and calm. We state what the product does and let it read as cleared rather than sold. We avoid fear language, exclamation, and buzzwords. One accent, one idea per line.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our designer built the original identity and left the company, and that working file left with him. What survives is a flat export of the mark on white and a phone photo of our trade show banner, neither of which is the source artwork. The mark needs to be rebuilt as usable artwork that sits correctly on our dark navy ground.
brand_identity.values: Trust earned through evidence, restraint over spectacle, clarity for a technical buyer, and claims that are cleared before they are spoken.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every claim card carries a 4 px Signal Cyan cursor rule beneath it that overruns the final letter by exactly one character width, like a terminal cursor that has stopped moving.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Sentinel Navy or Deep Slate and nothing else; Sentinel Navy is the main ground and always the ground behind the shield mark. The claim cards, the closing card and any lower third are Paper White; the product name is Paper White or Cloud Grey, as in the pale grey of the wordmark on the trade show banner; interface labels and fine print are Paper White or Cloud Grey. palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, type, rule or the mark, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the footage; any panel laid over a shot is solid Sentinel Navy or Deep Slate. Cuts and short dissolves between shots are transitions, not tints; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons; the supplied footage, and pure white #FFFFFF on the mark only, are the only exceptions. No second cyan rule in a frame, and no cyan type, ground, panel or icon. No glow, drop shadow, gradient, bevel, outline or metallic effect on any type, rule, panel or the mark: precision over spectacle.
palette_rules.photography: The screen captures and the office footage keep their own colour and are never recoloured toward the palette: no navy or cyan grade over the office clips. The dark navy chrome of the interface stays dark navy wherever it appears, in sentinelmesh_demo_raw_screen_01.mp4, sentinelmesh_demo_raw_screen_02.mp4, sentinelmesh_demo_raw_screen_03.mp4, and in sentinelmesh_still_02_lobby_wall.jpg or sentinelmesh_still_05_overshoulder.jpg if either is used: never lifted toward grey.
